name: Kyoto
short_description: Japan's old imperial capital, where wooden teahouses and Zen gardens sit beside neon arcades.
long_description: Spend mornings walking the bamboo grove at Arashiyama and afternoons drinking matcha in a centuries-old teahouse. Stay in a ryokan to sleep on tatami and bathe in mineral hot springs. Spring brings cherry blossoms; autumn turns the temples crimson.

name: Lisbon
tagline: Tiled hills above an Atlantic light
short_description: A seven-hill capital of pastel facades, custard tarts, and yellow trams climbing improbable slopes.
long_description: Walk the Alfama at dusk listening to fado spill from open windows. Eat fresh sardines grilled at street fairs and ride Tram 28 through the old quarters. Day trips reach Sintra's painted palaces and the surf beaches of Cascais.

name: Cape Town
short_description: Where Table Mountain crashes into the Atlantic, with vineyards, penguins, and Cape Malay cooking nearby.
long_description: Take the cable car up Table Mountain at sunrise and drive the coast to Cape Point. Wine-taste through Stellenbosch and Franschhoek, then end the day with fresh kingklip at the V&A Waterfront. Don't miss the African penguins at Boulders Beach.

name: Reykjavik
short_description: A small Nordic capital that's the launchpad for waterfalls, geysers, and glaciers in every direction.
long_description: Soak in the Blue Lagoon, drive the Golden Circle to see Geysir erupt, and chase the aurora borealis in winter. Summer brings the midnight sun and endless lupine fields. Eat fresh langoustines and try fermented shark if you dare.

name: Marrakech
tagline: A maze of color and spice
short_description: Red walls hide souks, palaces, and riads with secret gardens at the edge of the Atlas Mountains.
long_description: Lose yourself in the medina, bargain for lanterns and Berber rugs, and sip mint tea in a tiled courtyard. Watch sunset from a rooftop over Jemaa el-Fnaa as snake charmers and storytellers fill the square. Drive into the Atlas for Berber villages and waterfalls.

name: Queenstown
short_description: An alpine lake town surrounded by snowcapped peaks, vineyards, and every adrenaline sport invented.
long_description: Bungy jump where the sport was born, jet boat through canyons, or just sail Lake Wakatipu with a pinot noir in hand. Winter brings world-class skiing; summer opens hikes through Fiordland and Milford Sound. The night skies are dark enough to stargaze.

name: Istanbul
short_description: A Byzantine and Ottoman capital straddling Europe and Asia across the Bosphorus.
long_description: Walk under the dome of Hagia Sophia, haggle at the Grand Bazaar, and take a ferry across the Bosphorus at sunset. Drink Turkish coffee on cobblestones, eat baklava with pistachio cream, and bathe in a 500-year-old hammam. Every corner has a thousand-year story.

name: Buenos Aires
short_description: A grand European-style capital with a Latin pulse, where dinner starts at 10 and dancing lasts till dawn.
long_description: Eat asado in Palermo, watch tango under street lamps in San Telmo, and pay respects at Recoleta cemetery. Side trips reach the wineries of Mendoza and the falls of Iguazu. Bring stamina — the city doesn't sleep.

name: Bali
short_description: An Indonesian island of jungle temples, surf coasts, and yoga shalas built into volcanic hills.
long_description: Watch sunrise from Mount Batur, surf at Uluwatu, and sleep in a treehouse villa over the Ayung River. Ubud offers art markets and silent retreats; Canggu has beach clubs and digital nomads. Don't miss a Balinese dance performance at a cliffside temple.

name: Edinburgh
short_description: A volcanic-rock capital of stone closes and ghost stories, with the Highlands an hour north.
long_description: Climb Arthur's Seat at dawn, wander the medieval Royal Mile, and tour the castle perched over the city. Time your trip for the August festivals or Hogmanay if you can. Drive north to Glencoe, the Isle of Skye, and a single-malt distillery or three.

name: Petra
tagline: A rose-red city carved in stone
short_description: An entire Nabataean kingdom hand-carved into sandstone cliffs, hidden in the Jordanian desert.
long_description: Walk through the narrow Siq at dawn to see the Treasury glow. Climb to the Monastery for sweeping desert views. Combine with a night in Wadi Rum sleeping under a Milky Way so bright it casts shadows, then float in the Dead Sea on the way back.

name: Hoi An
short_description: A perfectly preserved trading port lit each night by thousands of silk lanterns over the Thu Bon River.
long_description: Have a suit tailored in a day, eat cao lau in a riverside cafe, and bike to An Bang beach. The full-moon lantern festival is unreal. Day trips reach the Cham ruins at My Son and the limestone karsts of Marble Mountains.

name: Banff
short_description: A Canadian Rockies town surrounded by glacial lakes, hot springs, and improbable mountain peaks.
long_description: Paddle on Lake Louise, drive the Icefields Parkway to the Columbia Glacier, and soak in the upper hot springs after a snowy day. Wildlife sightings — elk, bears, bighorn sheep — are common. Winter brings powder skiing at three nearby resorts.

name: Santorini
tagline: White cliffs over a sunken caldera
short_description: A volcanic Cycladic island of whitewashed villages spilling down cliffs into the Aegean.
long_description: Watch sunset from Oia, swim in the black-sand beaches of Perissa, and taste assyrtiko wine grown in volcanic ash. Take a boat to the hot springs at the caldera. Go shoulder season — high summer is crowded and hot.

name: Cusco
tagline: Inca capital in the high Andes
short_description: The launchpad for Machu Picchu and the Sacred Valley, with cobbled streets at 3,400 metres.
long_description: Acclimatize for two days with coca tea and chocolate before the Inca Trail or the train to Machu Picchu. Explore Sacsayhuaman, the Sacred Valley, and the rainbow mountains of Vinicunca. Try cuy if you're brave; pisco sours regardless.

name: Tbilisi
tagline: Wine, sulphur baths, and the Caucasus
short_description: A Caucasus capital of cobbled old quarters, wooden balconies, and 8,000 years of winemaking.
long_description: Soak in the sulphur baths of Abanotubani, eat khinkali and khachapuri until you can't move, and ride the cable car to the Mother of Georgia. Day trips reach Kazbegi's mountain monasteries and the Kakheti wine region.

name: Mexico City
short_description: A high-altitude megalopolis layered with Aztec pyramids, Spanish baroque, and the world's best taco stands.
long_description: Visit Teotihuacan at dawn, see Frida Kahlo's house in Coyoacan, and eat al pastor at midnight. Float on a trajinera through Xochimilco's canals on Sunday. The food scene is among the planet's best.

name: Chiang Mai
short_description: A walled northern Thai city of 300+ temples, mountain trails, and the gentlest elephant sanctuaries.
long_description: Wake before dawn for the monks' alms procession, learn to cook khao soi at a local school, and spend a day at the Elephant Nature Park. Trek the hills to Karen and Hmong villages. Time it for Yi Peng if you can — sky lanterns over the old city.

name: Dubrovnik
short_description: A walled medieval city on the Dalmatian coast with marble streets and turquoise sea on every side.
long_description: Walk the city walls at sunset, take the cable car up Mount Srdj, and ferry to Lokrum or the Elaphiti Islands for swimming. Eat black risotto and grilled fish at a harbour-side konoba. Go shoulder season — summer cruise crowds are intense.

name: Singapore
short_description: An island city-state where you can eat Michelin-starred chicken rice for $5 and sleep above the clouds.
long_description: Eat your way through Maxwell and Tiong Bahru hawker centres, swim in the rooftop infinity pool at Marina Bay Sands, and walk through the Cloud Forest at Gardens by the Bay. Don't miss the night safari and a Singapore sling at Raffles.

name: Salzburg
short_description: Mozart's birthplace at the foot of the Alps, with a fortress towering over a perfect old town.
long_description: Wander the Getreidegasse, tour Hohensalzburg Fortress, and take a Sound of Music day tour without irony. Eat a Salzburger Nockerl, then drive into the Salzkammergut lakes — Hallstatt is half an hour away. Winter brings Christmas markets and easy ski access.

name: Cartagena
short_description: A walled Spanish colonial port on the Caribbean, all bougainvillea, balconies, and ocean breeze.
long_description: Walk the walls at sunset, eat ceviche in Getsemani, and boat out to the Rosario Islands for a day of white sand and clear water. Stay in a colonial casa with a plunge pool in the courtyard. The nights are loud and warm.

name: Kathmandu
short_description: A chaotic, sacred capital of temples and prayer flags, with the world's tallest mountains an hour away.
long_description: Wander Durbar Square and the monkey temple, then fly to Lukla for the Everest Base Camp trek or to Pokhara for the Annapurnas. Eat dal bhat after every hike. The trekking is best in October-November.

name: Porto
short_description: A river-mouth city of azulejo-tiled churches and the cellars where every bottle of port matures.
long_description: Cross the Dom Luis I bridge at sunset, taste vintage tawnies in Vila Nova de Gaia, and ride the Douro Valley wine train through terraced vineyards. Eat francesinha if you're hungry — bring an appetite.

name: Seoul
short_description: A megacity where 600-year-old palaces sit beside neon-lit street food alleys and the world's best skincare.
long_description: Visit Gyeongbokgung at dawn, eat Korean barbecue in Mapo, and drink soju with strangers at a pojangmacha. Hike Bukhansan for skyline views. Take the KTX to Busan for beaches and seafood markets.

name: Marrakech to Sahara
short_description: The Erg Chebbi dunes near Merzouga — a Sahara experience reached by 4x4 from Marrakech or Fez.
long_description: Camel-trek into the dunes at golden hour, sleep in a Berber camp, and watch sunrise from the top of a 150m dune. Combine with Ait Benhaddou and the Atlas pass for a road trip Morocco won't let you forget.

name: Stockholm
short_description: A Nordic capital spread across an archipelago, all design shops, cinnamon buns, and waterside saunas.
long_description: Visit the Vasa Museum, take a ferry through the archipelago, and have fika in Sodermalm. Summer brings midnight light and outdoor concerts; winter brings glogg and the chance of snow on the cobbles.

name: Rio de Janeiro
short_description: A city wedged between rainforest mountains and Atlantic beaches, with Carnival in February.
long_description: Ride the tram to Christ the Redeemer, watch sunset from Sugarloaf, and spend an afternoon at Ipanema with a coco gelado. Hike the rainforest of Tijuca. Time it for Carnival or the off-season — both are unforgettable.

name: Hanoi
tagline: Old quarter pho and scooter chaos
short_description: Vietnam's atmospheric capital — French colonial architecture, lake-side temples, and the country's best pho.
long_description: Eat bun cha at a plastic stool on the sidewalk, walk around Hoan Kiem Lake at dawn, and weekend-trip to the karst seas of Ha Long Bay. The night train to Sapa puts you in the rice terraces by morning.

name: Tallinn
short_description: A walled medieval old town on the Baltic, half fairy tale and half digital-first European capital.
long_description: Walk the cobblestoned old town, taste black bread and elk soup, and sauna by the Baltic in winter. Day trip to Lahemaa National Park or ferry to Helsinki for the afternoon. Affordable, atmospheric, underrated.

name: Florence
short_description: Tuscany's stone capital, where Michelangelo's David stands in a hall and dinner is bistecca by candlelight.
long_description: Climb the Duomo, see the David at the Accademia, and watch sunset from Piazzale Michelangelo. Day trip through Chianti for wine and into Siena for the Palio. Eat ribollita and order the house wine.

name: Zanzibar
tagline: Spice islands on the Indian Ocean
short_description: A turquoise-water archipelago off the Tanzanian coast, blending Swahili, Arab, and Indian heritage.
long_description: Wander Stone Town's labyrinth, smell the spice farms, and sail a traditional dhow to Mnemba Atoll for snorkeling. Many travelers combine with a safari in the Serengeti or a Kilimanjaro climb on the mainland.

name: Vancouver
short_description: A Pacific Northwest city where you can ski in the morning and sail in the afternoon.
long_description: Bike around Stanley Park, take the SeaBus to North Van for the Capilano suspension bridge, and ferry to Vancouver Island for whale-watching off Tofino. Winter brings powder at Whistler; summer brings outdoor everything.

name: Luang Prabang
short_description: A UNESCO town at the Mekong-Khan confluence, where saffron-robed monks file at dawn through French colonial streets.
long_description: Watch the alms procession at sunrise, swim at Kuang Si waterfalls, and cruise the Mekong to the Pak Ou caves. Stay in a riverside guesthouse and let the days move slowly. Laos rewards patience.

name: Sevilla
short_description: Andalusia's heart — Moorish palaces, flamenco in tavernas, and orange trees lining every street.
long_description: Tour the Alcazar and the cathedral, see flamenco in a small tablao, and tapa-hop through Triana. April brings the Feria; spring scents the streets with azahar. Day trips reach Cordoba's Mezquita and the white villages of the Sierra.

name: Bergen
short_description: A rain-soaked Norwegian port of UNESCO wooden warehouses, with the world's most beautiful fjords just outside.
long_description: Take the Bryggen photo, ride the funicular up Floyen, and board the Norway in a Nutshell route through Naeroyfjord. Eat fresh salmon and brunost. Summer brings cruise ferries north toward the Lofoten Islands.

name: Sapporo
short_description: Hokkaido's capital — home to Japan's deepest powder, the world's best miso ramen, and February's snow festival.
long_description: Eat ramen at Susukino's Ramen Alley, ski Niseko's legendary powder, and visit the February ice-sculpture festival. Drive to Lake Toya, Furano's lavender fields, or the wild Shiretoko Peninsula.

name: Antigua
short_description: A Spanish colonial town of pastel facades and ruined churches, ringed by three active volcanoes.
long_description: Hike Volcan Acatenango overnight to watch Fuego erupt against the stars. Drink single-origin Guatemalan coffee, study Spanish for a week, and weekend-trip to Lake Atitlan. Visit during Semana Santa for processional carpets of dyed sawdust.

name: Bruges
short_description: A perfectly preserved medieval town of canals, belfries, and chocolatiers in West Flanders.
long_description: Boat through the canals, climb the belfry for the view, and drink Trappist beer at De Halve Maan brewery. Eat moules-frites and Belgian waffles without guilt. Stay overnight to have the town to yourself after the day-trippers leave.

name: Tasmania
tagline: Wild forests at the edge of the world
short_description: Australia's island state — UNESCO wilderness, dark-sky reserves, world-class whisky, and great food at every turn.
long_description: Hike Cradle Mountain, drink whisky in Hobart, and walk the Three Capes Track. Spot Tasmanian devils at Cradle and aurora australis from the south coast in winter. Tasmania is the wildness of New Zealand with the food scene of Melbourne.
